techniques.description: vertical push: the outgoing layout accelerates out of the top edge (ease-in, motion blur), hidden swap, the incoming layout rises from below the bottom edge and decelerates, with an opacity blink on the incoming element. This instance differs from v6c1's (f113-f153, replayed here at f1621-f1660) and the stored curves measure different things: v6.trans-push-up.v6c2 joins both halves into one in-out scroll in % H (bezier(0.811, -0.040, 0.000, 0.971) D=33), v6.trans-push-up.v6c1 is the incoming headline alone in px (ease-out spring, active 15 f), so neither can stand for the other as the technique's token. Half by half: the incoming halves agree (visible part 15 f in both: phone top 607 -> 54 px, within 2% of rest from f931, against v6c1's f138-f153); the outgoing halves differ (here a plain ease-in without an anticipation dip, -1/-4/-9/-21/-60 px per picture, 10 f to the swap; v6c1 first dips 36 px, v6.layout-anticipate-exit-up); 34 f against 41 f overall. The no-dip outgoing may make this a second technique
